notes: Corrected: 'there is' was carried on the predicate noun χάσμα under rule 96, but rule 96 says in terms that a clause carrying an expressed finite Greek verb is untouched by it. ἐστήρικται is an expressed perfect passive, so its English auxiliary and supplied expletive subject ride with it under rule 9, headed on 'fixed', and χάσμα keeps 'a … gulf'.
This also matches the chapter's own treatment of the existential at 16:1 and 16:19, where 'there was' rides with ἦν (rule 24).
